topic: Someone finds their grandmother's engagement ring in a pawn shop
text: I remember the worn, wooden box hidden beneath the old oak floor, its secrets tucked away with the dust of years. The ring, a cold circle of metal and stone, gleamed when I held it up, the light flickering through the trees. I didn’t think, just acted, driven by a need I couldn’t name. Now, seeing it in the harsh light of the pawn shop, the weight of metal heavy in my pocket, I can’t help but see the lines of her face, the way her hands would tremble when she spoke of it. I wonder how it got here, if anyone will miss it. The shop owner watches me, waiting, and I find myself reaching for my coat, the metal burning a hole in my pocket.
